To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the motor is able to withstand a temperature of 150°C for a period of time that is sufficient for most aerospace actuator applications.

the finite element analysis of a surface-mounted PM synchronous motor designed for aerospace applications was validated with measurements carried out under different conditions and that the finite element model can be used to accurately predict the temperature of the motor.

the finite-element thermal analysis of the surface-mounted permanent-magnetic synchronous motor is in good agreement with the experimental data and the thermal analysis can be used to predict the motor temperature at different operating conditions and duty cycles.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a finite-element package for thermal analysis of permanent-magnet synchronous machines.
the thermal investigation of an axial-flux permanent-magnet synchronous actuator designed for aerospace applications.
the development of a 3-D finite-element package for transient thermal analysis of surface-mounted permanent-magnetic synchronous machines for high-temperature actuation applications.

the developed thermal model is capable of predicting with good accuracy the motor temperature at the end of the test.

the finite-element model is able to predict accurately the temperature distribution of the actuator housing and the rotor, even under transient conditions, and it can be considered a valid tool for thermal design of high-temperature permanent-magnet synchronous motors.
the finite-element package is a very accurate tool for thermal analysis of permanent-magnet synchronous machines.

the thermal model is a powerful tool to predict the temperature distribution in a motor, and to optimize its design and operation for aerospace applications.
